b.v: original, then interpretive, then reproduction, then restrike
b.w: Comes first; a work counts as original when wholly made by hand.
Facts about the one work in hand, so shown as buying guidance only.
Judged by the artist, not the single work.

k.d: Pigment bound in a drying oil, on canvas, panel or a similar support.
Pigment bound in acrylic polymer emulsion.
A painting in which several paint media or added materials are used together and the image is painted, not built from pasted elements.
An image made mainly with aerosol or spray paint on canvas, panel or another support.
Transparent pigment in gum arabic, applied wet, normally on paper.
Opaque, chalk-bodied water-based colour, normally on paper.
Pigment bound in egg yolk or another egg or glue medium, usually on a prepared panel.
Black or coloured ink brushed in graded washes on paper or silk, in the East Asian manner.
Painting in ground mineral pigments fixed with animal glue, on paper or silk, in the Japanese tradition.
An image built in layers of natural or synthetic lacquer on a rigid panel, sanded and polished, often with inlaid shell or metal leaf.
Pigment in hot beeswax, fused to a support.
Pigment applied to wet or dry lime plaster, now removed from its wall.
A small painted portrait made as a work of its own, often on vellum, ivory, card or metal.
An image hand-painted in acrylic on a clear acetate sheet, made for an animated film.

b.w: Looked at after original against reproduction.
Forgery risk is stressed for Japanese and Chinese painting.

k.d: Lines bitten into a coated metal plate with acid.
Lines cut into a metal plate with a burin.
Lines scratched directly into a plate with a needle, without acid.
Tone made by acid biting through a porous ground of resin dust.
A plate roughened all over with a rocker, then burnished from dark to light.
An image cut with knives and gouges into the side grain of a wood block and printed from the raised surface.
An image cut into a linoleum sheet and printed from the raised surface.
An image cut with gravers into the end grain of a hardwood block.
Ink pushed through a mesh stencil, one stencil per colour.
An image drawn with a greasy medium on limestone and printed from the stone.
An image transferred from a plate through a rubber blanket to paper.
An image sprayed onto paper, canvas or another sheet by a print head with pigment or dye inks.
A single unique impression pulled from a painted or inked blank surface.
A unique impression from a reusable matrix, varied by inking or additions each time.
A print from a plate built up by gluing materials onto a board.
An image made by pressing damp paper into a carved or built-up plate so the design stands in relief, mainly without ink. Embossing added to an inked print is not this.

b.v: unique, then limited, then open; small (under 50) before large

b.m: Hand signature in pencil and numbering

b.w: Certificate, chop mark, blind stamp; facts about one edition.

b.v: bon a tirer; artist's proof (capped at about 10 percent of the edition); hors commerce
b.w: Set by the College Art Association print guidelines.

k.d: Silver halide in a gelatin layer on paper, exposed and developed in a darkroom.
Colour dyes formed in the layers of colour paper by development.
A pigment inkjet print of a photograph on fine-art paper.
Colour made by transferring dyes from matrices onto paper.
Colour dyes already in the paper, bleached away where not wanted.
An image on a silvered copper plate.
A positive image on a thin iron plate.
A collodion positive image on a glass plate, backed with a dark ground so the negative reads as a positive.
A self-developing print from an instant camera or film pack.
An image in platinum or palladium metal on paper.
An iron-salt print giving a blue image.
An image made without a camera by placing objects on light-sensitive material.

b.m: Process and print date against image date
b.w: A print made near the time of the picture is called a vintage print.

k.d: A figure or sculpture in porcelain or bone china.
A figure or sculpture in glazed fired clay other than porcelain.
Modelled or moulded clay fired without a glaze.
A blown, cast, fused or cut glass or lead-crystal figure or sculpture.

k.d: Cast copper-tin alloy, usually patinated.
Steel, iron or other ferrous metal welded, forged, cut or bent to form.
An ornamental figure cast in pewter, zinc, tin or another non-bronze metal.
Marble, limestone, alabaster or other stone carved to form.
A figure or sculpture carved from wood.
A figure or object carved from jade.
A figure or sculpture carved from ivory, bone, horn or antler.
A cast resin figure or sculpture, usually painted.
Cast or modelled plaster.
Modelled or cast wax.
A sculpture assembled from found, salvaged or discarded objects, or from several materials none of which governs.
A three-dimensional sculpture of fabric, fibre or other soft material, stuffed, wrapped or stitched.
A sculpture in which a lit gas-discharge tube or an equivalent light source is the medium.
A base, plinth or stand made for one sculpture.
An image drawn with graphite pencils.
An image drawn with charcoal.
An image drawn with pigment sticks (soft pastel, oil pastel) on paper or a similar ground.
An image drawn with pigmented pencils.
An image drawn with pen, nib or marker in ink.
A picture or pattern woven on a loom to hang on a wall.
A picture worked in thread with a needle on a fabric ground.
Writing made as the picture, in brush or pen script.
Script characters carved into a seal of stone or another material as a work of art, sold as the seal or its impressions.
A picture built from pasted or bonded elements (paper, cloth, photographs, found flat material).
A picture set in small pieces (tesserae) of stone, glass or ceramic.
A picture made by cutting one or more sheets of paper so the image is formed by the cuts, mounted for display (jianzhi, Scherenschnitte, kirie as named forms).
